rubrics.justification: Accurately identifies an expanded blastocyst with thinned zona, visible compact ICM on the left, and generally cohesive TE; appropriately notes image/focus limitations. Slightly overconfident calling TE fully A-grade from this single partially out-of-focus image.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, BMI, prior IVF outcomes including ectopic, sperm parameters, diagnosis, and endometrial thickness with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent: strong embryo and young age improve prognosis, while prior failures, ectopic history, BMI, and borderline lining temper estimates and guide recommendations.

Recommendations are largely evidence-based and consistent with IVF practice, including SET, caution about hydrosalpinx, and skepticism toward low-evidence add-ons. Minor soft spots include speculative comments on overexertion and broad endocrine labs without stronger case-specific indication.

Provides clear practical next steps for current transfer and future planning, including SET, luteal support review, tubal/cavity reassessment, early ectopic surveillance, and contingency planning if unsuccessful.
